questions.question: In which year did Niels Bohr propose a theory for the hydrogen atom based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities take only discrete values?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1913**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Niels Bohr:-**

 
 
• **He was a Danish physicist who made significant contributions to the development of atomic structure and quantum mechanics.**
 
• His theory for the hydrogen atom based on quantum theory is known as the Bohr model, which proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
 
• **In 1913 Niels Bohr proposed his theory for the hydrogen atom based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities take only discrete values.**
 
• Niels Bohr's theory proposed that electrons in an atom can only exist in certain energy levels, and when they move between levels, they emit or absorb energy in the form of photons.
 
• This theory helped to explain the spectral lines of hydrogen and paved the way for further development of quantum mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following has largest atomic radius?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Li.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lithium has the largest atomic radius i.e. **167pm.**
 
• Whereas, **Beryllium – 112 pm,** **Boron – 87 pm,** and **Oxygen – 48** pm are smaller than Lithium.
 
• Atomic radius is the measure of the size of the atom of a particular chemical element.
 
• The measurement from the center of the nucleus to the boundary of the surrounded electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Atomic radius - 

 
 
• It is the distance between the nucleus of an atom to its outermost electron that is called the 'Atomic Radius'.
 
• The exact value of the atomic radius of an atom cannot be known.
 
• Because the atom is not found in a free state nor can the exact position of the electron be known.​
 
• In general, the atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group.

options.text: NaCl has same equivalent weight and molecular weight.
H₂SO₄ has same equivalent weight and molecular weight.
CaCl₂ has same equivalent weight and molecular weight.
Na₂SO₄ has same equivalent weight and molecular weight

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Equivalent weight** - The weight of the substance that contains or reacts with 1.0078 g of hydrogen or 8 g of oxygen, or 35.45 g of chlorine.
 
• **Molecular weight** - Molecular mass is the sum of atomic masses of the elements present in a molecule. It is obtained by multiplying the atomic mass of each element by the number of its atoms and adding them together.

questions.question:
Isotopes have _______.

I. Similar physical quantities and different chemical properties

II. Different physical properties

III. Similar chemical properties
questions.solution:
Isotopes have different physical properties and similar chemical properties.

 
• They are the atoms of the same element having the same numbers of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• They have same chemical properties due to the same electronic configuration but different physical properties.

questions.question: Bohr’s model is related to which of the following?

options.text: The concept of quantization of energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The concept of quantization of energy.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Bohr’s model was presented by Niels Bohr and Ernest Rutherford in 1913 and is related to the concept of quantization of energy.
 
• According to the concept the atom is defined as a system consisting of a dense nucleus surrounded by revolving electrons.
 
• The Bohr model of the atom was put forth by Neil Bohr in 1915.
 
• According to this idea, negatively charged electrons in an atom move in defined circular orbits or shells that encircle the positively charged nucleus.
 
• - The energy of each orbit or shell is known.
 
• - The energy levels are denoted by the quantum number =1,2,3, etc. ), which is an integer. The nucleus side, which has the lowest energy level, is where this quantum number range starts.
 
• - The electrons of an atom can move from a lower energy level to a higher energy level by receiving the required energy, and from a higher energy level to a lower energy level by losing energy.
 
• Ernest Rutherford, a British scientist, conducted an experiment, and based on the findings, he suggested the atomic structure of the elements and developed the Rutherford Atomic Model (1911). The Thomson atomic model was developed in 1900, while the Bohr model of the atom was first proposed in 1915. As a result, it is the wrong choice.
